outcome.technical: (1) IDENTITY. plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py: _parts_below (a normcase string prefix) and _spelled_under are removed. In their place: _existing_head(path) gives the nearest existing directory and the names below it; _one_place(real, resolved) compares the write's folder parent and the config's folder parent with os.path.samestat. Where both parents exist, a folder name that differs only in case is judged by _case_walk from the folder's parent, so _one_entry and _volume_folds decide as before. Where a folder is missing, the heads are compared by samestat and only the tail below them is read as spelling. _names_audit_config's absent-config branch now calls _one_place. (2) THE TREE AS WRITTEN. _tree_as_spelled(directory, project) walks up from the written path's directory with lstat (_holds_repository) to the nearest ancestor holding .git. It returns that ancestor when it lies under the project (_under_directory, by samestat) or when its common git dir (_common_of: the .git dir, or a .git file's admin dir plus commondir, read with no process) is the project's. It returns None for another repository's .git and walks on past a .git that is no repository. audit_config_way adds that tree as a candidate for every config-named write (_config_named), wherever it lies. _session_tree also uses _tree_as_spelled(cwd, project) now, so path_tree no longer runs per write for the session. tree_for and path_tree are NOT touched. (3) NO PROCESS, NO LISTING. Measured by cf37/cf37b, which put a git shim on PATH and run the hook as a process. Git processes per hook run: in-project 0, in-project-new 0, in-nested 0, in-linked 2, in-linked-new 2, linked-on-project 0. These equal the aa4f320 tree's pinned ceilings; HEAD gives 0,0,0,3,3,2. The remaining 2 come from tree_for placing the path, which cf37 measures as its own column. Listings are 0 on every row. (4) THE GENERATED CASE. cf36 is built with itertools.product over named dimensions: whose 5 (project, session-tree, linked-out, nested-worktree, nested-repo), folder 5 (real, link-in, link-out, chain, dangling), present 2, form 2 (link, dest), level 8 (none, 0-6), session 2, tool 2 (Write, mcp). Seven named skip predicates. It ran 1430 arrangements, 1214 of them read by a loader. Per family: project 166, session-tree 166, linked-out 166, nested-worktree 456, nested-repo 476. Skipped: owner-is-project 320, session-tree-elsewhere 320, linked-out-standing-there 320, dangling-holds-nothing 224, dest-is-link 160, level-above-fixture 426, nothing-to-swap 0. It fails if any family ran none. Its oracle is the loader reading the written body for the project, the session's tree or the as-written tree; the guard is asked in process. cf36b runs the four measured arrangements as the hook process. cf36c is the agreement between process and in-process for one representative per family. On HEAD's code with these test files: cf36 has 174 disagreeing; cf36b, cf37 and cf29 fail; guard suite 122/126 and journal suite 170/171 (oq5b). After the change: guard 126/126 and journal 171/171. In tests/test_journal_writes.py, oq5 runs G.decide's hold against M.decide's config.edit over the same TGE.gen_sweep product. MCP arrangements are counted out by name (mcp-not-this-hooks-decide). oq5b runs the journal hook as a process over the measured Write arrangements. Its plain-folder row costs 32 disk calls against the 35 ceiling, and the walk adds no listing. The comment above cf29 says so. No other existing case was edited; cf31 stays as written because a folder case variant still reaches the stubbed _one_entry. (6) DOCUMENTS.
